title: Catalysis-induced condensates live on a consumed, regrowing fuel (SIE, new class): an enzyme with no reaction or decay term condenses from noise into ~200 droplets; stopping fuel regrowth at a fork dissolves every droplet within ~100 t on 2/2 seeds while total enzyme stays exactly constant, and a local feed cut kills the bodies inside it
summary: world.py is Cotton et al.'s catalysis-induced phase separation (enzyme e drifts up its own product p; e has no source, sink or decay; int e conserved to 1e-14) with the fuel F made a consumed field that regrows at kF=0.2 (chi=1, DF=1, y=1, lengths x3). From uniform e=0.15 plus noise, ~300 droplets form by t~300 on seeds 0-2 and coarsen slowly by merges to 184-192 by t=3000 (0 persistent splits; pack/). At a fork at t=1500 that sets kF=0 (pack_fork/, identical to the fed packs until then) fuel is exhausted within ~20 t and the body count falls 222->7->0 (seed 0) and 231->9->0 (seed 1) by t=1600-1700, while the fed twins keep 219/227 at t=1700; the e total line stays flat (timeseries.png), so the droplets dissolve, their enzyme is not destroyed. Local feed cuts around one seed-0 body (localcut.png): r=8.5 (2R) leaves it unchanged, r=17 shrinks it 55->42 px and it persists smaller, r=30 kills it by t=1700 together with the other bodies deep inside the disk, while bodies outside keep theirs. The reservoir twin (F held at 1, pack_hold/) and the chi=0 Laplacian-only twin (pack_chi0/, stays uniform) bracket the result. Limits: no division and no boundary layer; bodies are small (R_eq 3-4 px at Lsc=3) and coarsen without a size cap (see the companion finding).

claims.statement: In the fed world (seeds 0, 1, 2) enzyme droplets form from a uniform state plus noise and persist as discrete bodies (198-202 persistent tracks, median area ~41 px, single bodies keep a constant area for >1000 t between merges). They depend on the fuel they consume: when fuel regrowth stops at t=1500 every droplet dissolves within 100-200 t on seeds 0 and 1, while in the fed twins (identical until the fork) the same droplets live on; when the feed is cut only in a disk of radius 30 around one body, that body and those deep in the disk dissolve and those outside persist. The enzyme has no reaction or decay term, so the dependence is not imposed on the body matter; it comes from catalysis holding the condensate together.
claims.track: seed 0, the body centred at (y,x)=(130,133), area 55 px at t=1500 (centre of localcut.png): alive from t~300 to t=3000 at 54-55 px in the fed pack (pack/seed0), gone by t~1600-1700 in pack_fork/seed0 and pack_cut30, shrunk to 42 px but alive in pack_cut17

controls_run.E: pack_fork/seed0 and seed1 (kF=0 everywhere from t=1500, WORLD_P fork_t=1500) against pack/seed0 and pack/seed1: 222->0 and 231->0 bodies by t=1700 vs 219 and 227 fed; pack_cut8, pack_cut17, pack_cut30 (kF=0 in a disk of radius 8.5/17/30 around the track body from t=1500, seed 0): body area at t=2500 = 54 / 42 / 0 px vs 54 fed, bodies outside the disk unaffected (217 vs 219 total at t=1700)

claims.bd_control: pack_chi0 (chi=0: the drift replaced by nothing, enzyme only diffuses, same rates otherwise): no bodies ever form (0 components). Trivial: CIPS needs the drift.
